name: Duke
note: Duke transfer applicants apply to one of exactly two undergraduate schools — Trinity College of Arts & Sciences or the Pratt School of Engineering — and the split is brutally lopsided: for the Fall 2026 class Duke admitted 147 of 2,443 transfer applicants (6% campus-wide), of whom 132 went to Trinity and only 15 to Pratt (8 enrolling). Duke's saving grace is that there is no second gate: once you are in Trinity you may declare any Trinity major, including Computer Science, with no internal application. Duke has no undergraduate business degree at all (Fuqua is graduate-only), and its only BSN is an accelerated second-degree program outside undergraduate admissions.

majors.name: Trinity College of Arts & Sciences
prereqs: Full-time coursework at an accredited college
SAT or ACT scores required of transfer applicants
High school transcript plus all college transcripts
March 15 deadline; decisions mid-May
majors.note: This is the big open college and absorbs roughly 90% of Duke's transfer admits (132 of 147 in the most recent cycle), but the campus-wide transfer rate is still only about 6%, so 'open' here means open relative to Pratt, not easy.

majors.name: Pratt School of Engineering
prereqs: Calculus required as a prerequisite for admission
Physics strongly recommended
SAT or ACT scores required
March 15 deadline
majors.note: Pratt took just 15 of Duke's 147 transfer admits and enrolled 8, so an engineering transfer applicant is competing for a single-digit number of seats and must already have calculus done — Duke publishes no separate Pratt transfer rate, but the admit count makes it the hardest door on campus.

majors.name: Computer Science (Trinity)
prereqs: Admission to Trinity College is the only gate
No secondary or internal application to declare the CS major
Calculus recommended for the B.S. track
majors.note: Unlike Berkeley, UT Austin, or UW, Duke does not gate CS behind a secondary admission — CS lives in Trinity and any admitted Trinity student can declare it, so all of the difficulty is concentrated in the Trinity transfer decision itself.

majors.name: Economics (Trinity)
prereqs: Admission to Trinity College is the only gate
No secondary application to declare the major
Introductory micro- and macroeconomics transfer toward the major
majors.note: Economics is Duke's de facto business major and is freely declarable inside Trinity — applicants hunting for an undergraduate business school should know Duke does not have one, since Fuqua admits graduate students only.

majors.name: Accelerated BSN, Duke School of Nursing
prereqs: Completed bachelor's degree in another field required
Prerequisite science coursework set by the School of Nursing
Not part of Duke's undergraduate transfer application
majors.note: There is no traditional undergraduate nursing transfer path at Duke — the only BSN is a second-degree accelerated program for applicants who already hold a bachelor's, so a community college nursing hopeful cannot transfer into it.

name: Emory
note: Emory is genuinely transfer-friendly at the arts-and-sciences level — the university states its transfer admit rate has historically run about 20–25%, with roughly 100–120 transfers enrolling per year — but the destination matters. Applicants choose Emory College of Arts and Sciences or the Goizueta Business School on the same application; the Nell Hodgson Woodruff School of Nursing runs an entirely separate BSN Transfer Option application with its own prerequisite list; and Oxford College, the two-year Atlanta-area campus, takes first-year students only. Emory College imposes no secondary admission on any of its majors, so CS is reachable for anyone admitted.

majors.name: Emory College of Arts and Sciences
prereqs: Minimum 28 graded college credit hours completed or in progress
AP, IB, and dual-enrollment credit do not count toward the 28 hours
Minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA; admitted students typically 3.5+
Maximum 62 transfer hours; four semesters must be completed at Emory
majors.note: This is the main and most accessible door — Emory publishes a historical 20–25% transfer admit rate range rather than a single figure, and the 28-hour floor means you generally cannot apply straight out of high school on AP credit alone.

majors.name: Computer Science (Emory College)
prereqs: Admission to Emory College is the only gate
No secondary or internal application to declare the CS major
Calculus and introductory CS coursework transfer toward the major
majors.note: CS at Emory has no capacity screen once you are admitted to the College, which makes Emory one of the more realistic private-university targets for a transfer student who wants CS but is locked out of impacted programs elsewhere; note Emory has no engineering school of its own and offers engineering only through a dual-degree arrangement with Georgia Tech.

majors.name: Goizueta Business School (BBA)
prereqs: 28 graded credit hours completed or in progress, excluding AP/IB/dual enrollment
Minimum 3.0 GPA; most admits at 3.5 or better
Little or no prior business coursework preferred
Must enter early enough to complete the BBA core at Emory
majors.note: Goizueta admits a small transfer cohort and prefers students who enter by sophomore year with their business coursework still ahead of them — paradoxically, a community college applicant who already stacked accounting, finance, and management courses is a weaker candidate, not a stronger one.

majors.name: Nell Hodgson Woodruff School of Nursing (BSN Transfer Option)
prereqs: 60 semester hours of graded credit before starting
Gen Chem I, A&P I and II, and Microbiology, all with lab, plus Nutrition
Introductory Statistics and Human Growth/Life Span Development
No pass/fail on prerequisites; A&P within 7 years; TEAS/SAT/ACT/GRE required if GPA is under 3.5
majors.note: This is a purpose-built junior-entry transfer pathway rather than an afterthought — you finish four prerequisite semesters elsewhere and four nursing semesters at Emory — but admission depends on both competitiveness and clinical space availability, and a single pass/fail prerequisite grade can disqualify you.

majors.name: Oxford College
prereqs: First-year entry only
Oxford does not accept transfer applications
majors.note: Students sometimes assume Oxford is the easier back door into Emory, but it admits only incoming freshmen; transfers must apply directly to Emory College, Goizueta, or Nursing.

name: Georgetown
note: Georgetown is one of the strictest school-level admits in the country: transfer applicants must apply directly to one of Georgetown's undergraduate schools AND declare a specific major on the application, and moving between schools after enrolling requires a separate internal transfer process. The campus-wide transfer rate has run roughly 13–17% (296 admitted of 2,241 applicants for Fall 2023), but no school-level transfer rates are published — the freshman-cycle rates by school that circulate online are not transfer rates. Three programs are outright closed to transfer applicants: American Studies, Business and Global Affairs, and International Business, Language, and Culture. Deadline is March 1 with decisions by June 1, and SAT/ACT is required if you finished high school within the past five years.

majors.name: Georgetown College of Arts & Sciences
prereqs: Apply directly to the school and declare a major on the application
SAT or ACT required if you left high school within the past five years
March 1 deadline; decisions by June 1
American Studies is closed to transfer applicants
majors.note: The College admits the largest number of transfers of any Georgetown school and is the realistic target for most applicants, but the roughly 13% campus-wide transfer rate is the only published figure — Georgetown does not release per-school transfer numbers.

majors.name: Computer Science (College of Arts & Sciences)
prereqs: Admission to the College of Arts & Sciences is the only gate
No secondary application to declare CS after enrolling
Calculus and introductory programming coursework recommended
majors.note: Georgetown has no engineering school and no capacity cap on CS, so the major is declarable once you are admitted to the College — the entire contest is the College transfer decision, not a departmental screen.

majors.name: Walsh School of Foreign Service
prereqs: Foreign language proficiency required to earn the SFS degree
Micro- and macroeconomics recommended before transferring
History and government coursework aligned with the SFS core
Business and Global Affairs and IBLC are closed to transfers
majors.note: SFS expects a demonstrated commitment to international affairs and, critically, a language proficiency requirement you must clear to graduate — a transfer who arrives with no language sequence started is signing up for a hard scramble in two years.

majors.name: McDonough School of Business
prereqs: At least one completed semester of 12 or more transferable credits
Microeconomics and macroeconomics recommended
Calculus recommended; statistics helpful
IBLC and Business and Global Affairs closed to transfers
majors.note: McDonough's business core is rigid and sequenced, so transfer seats are few and effectively limited to sophomore-year entrants who have already cleared micro, macro, and calculus — arriving as a junior usually cannot be made to fit.

majors.name: School of Nursing
prereqs: Human Anatomy & Physiology I and II
Chemistry
Liberal arts coursework aligned with the Georgetown Core
100- and 200-level courses from the BSN curriculum guide
majors.note: Nursing transfers are constrained by clinical cohort capacity, not just academic review, so you must both hit the anatomy/physiology and chemistry prerequisites and enter early enough to complete the full clinical sequence in residence.

majors.name: School of Health
prereqs: Liberal arts coursework aligned with the Georgetown Core
Biology and chemistry recommended for Human Science applicants
Declare a specific major on the application
March 1 deadline
majors.note: The School of Health (Human Science, Global Health, Health Care Management & Policy) is a distinct admitting unit from both Nursing and the College, and because you commit to a named major at application, a Human Science applicant without college bio and chem reads as underprepared.

name: NYU
note: NYU transfer applicants apply to one specific school or college, and NYU maintains a dedicated 'Additional Program Requirements for External Transfers' page precisely because the prerequisite and portfolio rules differ school by school. The campus-wide transfer rate is far more forgiving than the roughly 8-9% first-year rate, but it averages across a nearly prerequisite-free College of Arts and Science and a fall-only, prerequisite-gated Stern. NYU does not publish admit rates by school or major, and widely circulated 'sub-5% by school' figures found on third-party sites are unverified — no major-level percentages are reported here for that reason. Across all schools, a maximum of 64 credits transfer and credit requires a C or better with no pass/fail.

majors.name: College of Arts and Science
prereqs: No required prerequisites for any CAS program
Major-relevant coursework reviewed closely
Maximum 64 transferable credits
Grade of C or better; no pass/fail credit
majors.note: CAS is the big open door — it explicitly has no prerequisites for any of its majors, so a strong GPA in courses relevant to your intended major is the whole case, and it is the sensible application target for anyone unsure they can clear Stern's or Tandon's course gates.

majors.name: Tandon School of Engineering — Computer Science, B.S.
prereqs: Precalculus-level math completed in high school or college (required minimum)
College-level calculus (most competitive applicants have it)
Physics recommended for CS; required for Applied Physics and Mechanical Engineering
Prerequisite course details submitted via the NYU Applicant Portal
majors.note: Tandon's floor is only precalculus, which makes it look accessible, but the realistic admitted profile has college calculus already finished — and you must report your calculus, chemistry and physics coursework through the applicant portal, so gaps are visible.

majors.name: Leonard N. Stern School of Business
prereqs: Calculus I, II or III completed with a letter grade (no pass/fail)
Writing/composition
Microeconomics, statistics/regression and financial accounting for junior-year entry
Fall entry only
majors.note: Stern is the hardest school at NYU to transfer into: it considers external transfers for fall only, the prerequisites must be finished in letter-graded courses, and junior-year entrants need the full econ-stats-accounting block done before they apply.

majors.name: Rory Meyers College of Nursing
prereqs: Chemistry (CHEM-UA 120 equivalent)
Nutrition (NUTR-UE 119 equivalent)
Developmental/child psychology (APSY-UE 1271 equivalent)
All nursing prerequisites completed with C or better
majors.note: Meyers runs two distinct tracks — 'traditional transfer' for students without a bachelor's and 'second degree transfer' for those who already hold one — and clinical cohort capacity, not just your GPA, caps how many transfers can be taken in any term.

majors.name: Tisch School of the Arts
prereqs: Artistic review: portfolio, audition or creative submission by program
Program-specific supplemental materials
Maximum 64 transferable credits
Grade of C or better; no pass/fail credit
majors.note: The artistic review, not the transcript, decides Tisch — and because studio training is sequenced from the first year, some programs admit transfers only into specific entry points or not at all in a given cycle.

majors.name: Steinhardt School of Culture, Education, and Human Development
prereqs: Program-specific portfolio or audition for music, art and performing arts programs
Major-relevant prerequisite coursework by program
Maximum 64 transferable credits
Grade of C or better; no pass/fail credit
majors.note: Steinhardt spans everything from education to music performance, so 'transferring to Steinhardt' means nothing until you name the program — the audition-based ones behave like Tisch while the education and applied-psychology ones behave much more like CAS.

name: UC Merced
note: UC Merced is by far the most open UC for transfers — the UC system's official transfer admit data page reports 6,635 applicants and 5,089 admits for the most recent cycle (67.5% campus-wide), with ~97% of admitted transfers coming from California community colleges. But admission is still decided at the school/major level: each of the three schools sets its own minimum transfer GPA (Engineering 3.0, Natural Sciences 2.9, Social Sciences/Humanities/Arts 2.8, with Psychology and Public Health carrying a raised 3.0), and every major in all three schools requires specific lower-division major preparation completed by the end of spring for fall entry. UC Merced does not publish admit rates broken out by individual major, and it has no undergraduate nursing program (Public Health is the closest analog). No major-level percentages are reported here because none are published.

majors.name: Computer Science and Engineering, B.S.
prereqs: CSE 20 and CSE 21 equivalents with a grade of B or better
Calculus I and II
Additional required math (discrete/linear algebra per articulation)
School of Engineering minimum 3.0 transfer GPA
majors.note: This is UC Merced's tightest screen — the two programming courses must be done with B or better, not the usual C, so a student with a C in intro CS is effectively out even at a campus admitting two-thirds of transfers.

majors.name: Mechanical Engineering, B.S.
prereqs: Calculus I, II and III
Calculus-based physics (mechanics and E&M) with lab
General chemistry
School of Engineering minimum 3.0 transfer GPA
majors.note: The full calculus-plus-physics sequence must be finished by the end of spring term, so the sequencing at your community college — not your GPA — is usually what decides whether you are eligible this cycle or next.

majors.name: Biological Sciences, B.S.
prereqs: General biology series with lab
General chemistry with lab
Organic chemistry (per articulation)
School of Natural Sciences minimum 2.9 transfer GPA
majors.note: A genuinely reachable path for a solid community college science student — the bar is completing the lab science sequence, not out-competing a large applicant pool.

majors.name: Psychology, B.A.
prereqs: Introductory psychology
Statistics
Required major preparation courses with C or better
Minimum 3.0 transfer GPA (raised above the 2.8 SSHA floor)
majors.note: Psychology is the one high-demand major inside the otherwise open SSHA school, and it carries the same 3.0 GPA minimum as Engineering — do not assume the school's 2.8 applies to you.

majors.name: Management and Business Economics, B.S.
prereqs: Microeconomics and macroeconomics
Calculus for business/social science
Statistics
School of SSHA minimum 2.8 transfer GPA
majors.note: UC Merced's business-facing major is unusually accessible compared to business programs at other UCs, but the econ and calculus preparation is still required, not merely recommended.

majors.name: School of Social Sciences, Humanities and Arts (humanities and arts majors)
prereqs: Major preparation courses with C or better
Minimum 2.8 transfer GPA
60 semester/90 quarter transferable units
UC transfer course pattern (English composition and math)
majors.note: This is the big open college and the realistic fallback for anyone screened out of Engineering — the 2.8 floor plus completed major prep is the whole gate, and a TAG agreement can lock in admission before you apply.

name: UPenn

majors.name: Wharton School (Business/Economics)
prereqs: At least one calculus course completed in the first year of college (a second may be required after credit evaluation)
Both introductory microeconomics and macroeconomics (or 5s on both AP Econ exams, or IB HL Economics 6-7)
Two semesters of college-level foreign language, or equivalent placement/test scores
Must apply as a second-year transfer with exactly one year of credit; must name an intended concentration
majors.note: Wharton is the hardest door at Penn and admits essentially only rising sophomores, so a student who already has two years of credit is ineligible no matter how strong the record.

majors.name: Penn Engineering (SEAS) — incl. Computer Science
prereqs: Two calculus courses
One calculus-based physics course (a second strongly recommended for BE, CMPE, MEAM, MSE)
One chemistry course (two recommended for BE, CBE, MSE)
One computer programming course
majors.note: SEAS also admits only second-year transfers and requires you to pick a specific BSE or BAS major on the application, so the full first-year math/science/programming sequence must already be done or in progress.

majors.name: School of Nursing (BSN)
prereqs: Minimum of eight transferable college courses
Introduction to Chemistry with lab
Introduction to Biology with lab
Anatomy and Physiology I with lab (or Human Anatomy with lab)
majors.note: Nursing accepts both second- and third-year transfers but everyone enters as a second-year student regardless of credits, so plan on three more years and get microbiology, A&P II, nutrition, and statistics done to stay on the clinical sequence.

majors.name: College of Arts and Sciences
prereqs: No school-specific course prerequisites beyond strong college coursework
Transferable courses must be from a regionally accredited institution, passed with C or better, and comparable in content/credit hours
Second- or third-year transfer entry permitted
Roughly one full year of college credit minimum
majors.note: The College is the widest door at Penn — no extra academic screen and it accepts third-year transfers — but Penn's transfer admit rate is still in the low single digits, and once admitted to a school you cannot switch schools afterward, so the school you apply to is effectively permanent.

note: Penn transfer admission is decided at the undergraduate-school level: you apply directly into the College of Arts and Sciences, Penn Engineering, Nursing, or Wharton, and Penn states that a transfer admitted to one school cannot later transfer between schools. Wharton and Engineering take only second-year transfers; the College and Nursing also take third-year transfers. Penn does not publish transfer admit rates broken out by school, so no per-school percentage should be quoted.

name: USC
note: USC admits transfers to a specific school, and the school's own faculty requirements drive the decision — the campus-wide transfer rate (2,310 admits from 9,488 applicants, roughly 24% in the most recently reported cycle) hides a very wide spread. USC's published transfer profile reports Marshall as about 23% of admitted transfers and Viterbi about 11%, but those are shares of the admitted class, not admit rates, and USC does not publish admit rates by school or major. Transfers are expected to have around 30 transferable units and the mid-50% admitted GPA has run roughly 3.7-4.0. USC has no undergraduate nursing program, so nursing-bound transfers should look elsewhere. No major-level percentages are reported here because none are published.

majors.name: Viterbi School of Engineering — Computer Science, B.S.
prereqs: Calculus I and II (MATH 125/126 equivalents)
Programming coursework (may substitute for lab science for CS majors)
USC writing requirement equivalent (WRIT 150)
Two additional Viterbi-specific essay prompts
majors.note: Viterbi publicly states it admits at a rate similar to the university overall, but CS is the single most oversubscribed major inside it — and students who already have Calc I and II should take Linear Algebra (MATH 225 equivalent) rather than Calc III, which is not in the CS curriculum.

majors.name: Marshall School of Business — Business Administration, B.S.
prereqs: College writing (WRIT 150 equivalent)
Business calculus (MATH 118 equivalent)
Microeconomics and macroeconomics
Financial and managerial accounting (two semesters, strongly encouraged)
majors.note: Marshall takes the largest single share of USC's transfer class, so it is a real target rather than a lottery — but applications are only considered once the writing and business calculus prerequisites are actually complete, so an in-progress calculus course can sink an otherwise strong file.

majors.name: Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
prereqs: USC writing requirement equivalent (WRIT 150)
Progress toward USC General Education categories
Approximately 30 transferable units
Major-relevant lower-division coursework per articulation history
majors.note: Dornsife is the large, comparatively open college and the standard route in for humanities, social science and pre-health transfers — the emphasis is on GPA and completed GE/writing rather than a narrow prerequisite gauntlet.

majors.name: Jimmy Iovine and Andre Young Academy
prereqs: SlideRoom portfolio submission
Supplemental Academy application
Interview by invitation
Academy-specific essays
majors.note: The Academy enrolls only a few dozen students per class total and fills essentially all seats at the first-year level, so external transfer admission is rare to nonexistent in most cycles — treat it as a long shot, not a plan.

majors.name: School of Cinematic Arts
prereqs: Creative portfolio / supplemental materials via SlideRoom
Program-specific writing samples
USC writing requirement equivalent
Approximately 30 transferable units
majors.note: Admission is driven by the creative portfolio review rather than by GPA, and transfer seats are limited by how many students the program's production sequences can absorb mid-stream.

majors.name: Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism
prereqs: USC writing requirement equivalent (WRIT 150)
Introductory communication or journalism coursework per articulation
Progress toward USC General Education
Approximately 30 transferable units
majors.note: Annenberg is materially more selective than Dornsife but does not require a portfolio — the differentiator is demonstrated media, writing or journalism work alongside a high transferable GPA.

name: Vanderbilt

majors.name: College of Arts and Science
prereqs: At least 12 semester hours of post-high-school college credit to count as a transfer
Official high school transcript plus transcripts from every college attended
Two academic letters of recommendation, preferably at least one from a college instructor
No school-specific course prerequisites
majors.note: A&S is Vanderbilt's largest undergraduate school with 46 majors and the only unit with no additional application requirements, making it the most realistic target for a transfer without a heavy STEM or audition record.

majors.name: College of Connected Computing (computing / AI)
prereqs: No additional application items listed beyond the standard transfer file
Strong quantitative record; computing coursework expected for advanced standing
At least 12 semester hours of transferable college credit
Second bachelor's degree candidates are generally not eligible
majors.note: This is Vanderbilt's newest undergraduate college and is now a selectable option on the transfer application — confirm with admissions which unit actually houses your intended computing degree, since CS degrees have historically been offered through Engineering (B.S.) and Arts and Science (B.A.).

majors.name: School of Engineering
prereqs: College-level calculus
Calculus-based physics
College chemistry
Courses must be completed or in progress at the time of admission
majors.note: Vanderbilt states plainly that a strong background in college-level physics, calculus, and chemistry is critical and expects admitted transfers to have finished that sequence, so a transfer without it will either be denied or lose a year.

majors.name: Peabody College (incl. Human and Organizational Development)
prereqs: Must specify an intended major on the application
Demonstrated fit with that specific major
At least 12 semester hours of transferable credit
Second bachelor's degree candidates are not eligible
majors.note: Peabody says outright that your fit for the intended major and the space available in that major weigh heavily in the decision, which makes HOD — Vanderbilt's de facto pre-business major — a capacity-limited target rather than an open one.

majors.name: Blair School of Music
prereqs: Separate Blair School of Music application
Prescreening video
Repertoire list and music resume
Artistic letters of recommendation
majors.note: Blair is an audition-gated conservatory admission on top of the university transfer review, so the musical prescreen, not the GPA, is the real filter.

note: Vanderbilt transfer applicants apply to one of five undergraduate schools — Arts and Science, Connected Computing, Engineering, Peabody, or Blair — and the requirements diverge sharply by school. Vanderbilt has no undergraduate nursing or undergraduate business degree (the School of Nursing is graduate-entry; HOD in Peabody is the business-adjacent option). Vanderbilt does not publish transfer admit rates by school, and third-party figures floating around for the campus-wide transfer rate conflict, so none is quoted here.

name: Wisconsin
note: UW-Madison admits transfers to the university with a required first- and second-choice major, and a first choice in the School of Business or College of Engineering must be paired with a second choice outside both; engineering transfers are considered for direct admission to their major through the Office of Admissions, Business requires a separate pre-business application and is closed to direct transfer from outside Wisconsin institutions, Nursing runs its own School of Nursing application on a separate timeline, and majors like Computer Sciences are entered by post-enrollment declaration rather than at admission.

majors.name: College of Letters & Science
prereqs: 24 transferable semester hours of college-level work completed after high school graduation
AP, A-Level, IB, and CLEP cannot be used toward the 24-credit minimum
No freshman-level transfers — UW-Madison does not admit below sophomore standing
No published minimum GPA; GPA is reviewed for the university and for the intended major
majors.note: L&S is the default landing spot and the mandatory second choice for direct-entry applicants, since admissions.wisc.edu requires a Business or Engineering first choice to be paired with a second choice outside both, so students denied a direct-entry program are frequently still admitted to UW-Madison through L&S.

majors.name: Computer Sciences (College of Letters & Science)
prereqs: Admission to UW-Madison / L&S (24 transferable credits)
Credit for COMP SCI 300 and MATH 222 (Calculus and Analytic Geometry 2)
Grade of BC or higher in COMP SCI 300, COMP SCI/E C E 354, or COMP SCI 400, taken at UW-Madison
2.250 GPA or higher among major-declaration-eligible coursework
majors.note: Declaration is requirement-based rather than a capped competitive review and the GPA bar is only 2.250, but the trap for transfers is that the BC-or-higher qualifying course must be taken at UW-Madison, so a transferred CS2 course will not satisfy it and most transfers need a semester on campus before declaring.

majors.name: College of Agricultural and Life Sciences
prereqs: 24 transferable semester hours (university-wide transfer minimum)
Select a CALS major as the first choice on the UW-Madison application
No CALS-specific prerequisite courses or supplemental application
At least 30 credits must ultimately be earned at UW-Madison to graduate from CALS
majors.note: The Guide states flatly that CALS majors do not have enrollment caps and that transfer students are admitted directly to CALS by listing a CALS major first, making it the most open door at UW-Madison for a science-leaning transfer.

majors.name: Wisconsin School of Business (BBA)
prereqs: Communications
Calculus
Economics (in-progress courses must be finished by the end of the application term)
3.0 minimum GPA at the time of application and at the conclusion of the spring term
majors.note: Direct transfer into the BBA is fall-entry only and open only to students coming from Universities of Wisconsin, Wisconsin Technical College, or Wisconsin Tribal College institutions — applicants from private or out-of-state schools must first enroll at UW-Madison and complete a minimum of 12 in-residence credits before applying via the separate pre-business application (resume, essay, Pre-Business 101 workshop), which is completed in early March preceding the intended fall term.

majors.name: Mechanical Engineering (College of Engineering)
prereqs: Apply to the Office of Admissions with Mechanical Engineering as first choice plus a second choice outside Business and Engineering
24 transferable semester hours of college-level work
Math course sequence through MATH 222 (Calculus and Analytic Geometry 2)
Introduction to Engineering course specified by the degree program plus four foundational math/engineering courses (progression requirement)
majors.note: The College's cross-campus page states that "Due to high student demand, Mechanical Engineering has been especially selective in recent semesters," and the Core/Overall GPA thresholds that actually gate progression into the major are maintained on an internal page rather than published, so no verified numeric bar exists for ME.

majors.name: Computer Engineering (College of Engineering)
prereqs: Apply to the Office of Admissions with Computer Engineering as first choice plus a second choice outside Business and Engineering
24 transferable semester hours of college-level work
Math course sequence through MATH 222 (Calculus and Analytic Geometry 2)
Introduction to Engineering course specified by the degree program plus four foundational math/engineering courses (progression requirement)
majors.note: UW-Madison publishes no per-major Core or Overall GPA number for Computer Engineering — the Guide only says these requirements are "defined by CoE departments for each engineering degree program" behind an internal link — so any specific figure circulating online (such as a 3.2 Core / 2.5 Overall split) should be treated as unverified.

majors.name: Civil Engineering (College of Engineering)
prereqs: Apply to the Office of Admissions with Civil Engineering as first choice plus a second choice outside Business and Engineering
24 transferable semester hours of college-level work
Math course sequence through MATH 222 (Calculus and Analytic Geometry 2)
Introduction to Engineering course specified by the degree program plus four foundational math/engineering courses (progression requirement)
majors.note: Civil is commonly treated as one of the more accessible engineering doors at UW-Madison, but the college publishes neither per-major admit rates nor per-major GPA thresholds; the only published numeric floor anywhere is a 2.500 Core GPA below which cross-campus applicants are not considered without an appeal.

majors.name: Nursing, BSN (Traditional) — School of Nursing
prereqs: Human Anatomy (ANAT&PHY 337) and Human Physiology (ANAT&PHY 235 or ANAT&PHY 335)
Chemistry (CHEM 103, 108, or 109) and Microbiology (MICROBIO 101, CHEM 343, or NUTR SCI 332)
Psychology (PSYCH 202), a Sociology/Anthropology social science course, and Human Growth & Development (ED PSYCH 320/321/331, HDFS 262/263, or PSYCH 460/464)
2.75 cumulative and 2.75 prerequisite GPA, with C or higher in at least four of the seven prerequisites by the mid-January deadline and in all seven before admission
majors.note: Nursing requires a second, separate School of Nursing application due mid-January for a fall start with decisions on or before July 1, on top of UW-Madison admission, and eligibility is restricted to applicants who "have not previously enrolled in a professional Bachelor of Science-Nursing program at another institution" — so a student already in a BSN program elsewhere is barred outright.

name: Yale

majors.name: Yale College (single admission pool, all majors)
prereqs: One to two years of transferable college credit at the time of application
Grades of A or B in at least three-quarters of transferable courses, nothing below C
Pass/Fail coursework generally does not transfer
Transfer Common Application, college report, academic evaluations, and transcripts by March 1
majors.note: Yale admits one small transfer cohort to Yale College as a whole — 34 transfer students enrolled in fall 2025 — with no per-major or per-school quotas, so intended major does not change your odds and the campus-level pool is the entire story.

majors.name: Computer Science
prereqs: No separate major application; the major is declared after enrolling
Yale's introductory CS gateway course must be completed before upper-level electives
Calculus and linear algebra for the B.S. track
Departmental review of any transferred CS credit toward the major
majors.note: Unlike Penn or Vanderbilt, wanting CS at Yale carries no admissions penalty at all — the only friction is fitting the intro sequence and prerequisite chain into the semesters you have left.

majors.name: Engineering B.S. programs (Yale SEAS)
prereqs: Multivariable calculus
Calculus-based physics sequence
General chemistry for biomedical and chemical tracks
Transferred science/math credit must be approved by the department
majors.note: There is no separate engineering admission, but the accredited B.S. sequences are long enough that a transfer entering with junior standing and without calculus and physics done often cannot finish on time — an advising problem, not an admissions one.

majors.name: Majors requiring a sophomore-year departmental application (e.g. Global Affairs)
prereqs: A separate departmental application filed during sophomore year at Yale
Specific prerequisite courses that vary by department
Contact the Director of Undergraduate Studies immediately after being offered admission
majors.note: Yale explicitly warns transfers entering with second-semester sophomore or junior standing to reach out to the DUS right away, because a handful of majors gate entry through an internal sophomore-year application whose window a transfer can easily miss.

majors.name: Economics
prereqs: Introductory microeconomics and macroeconomics
At least one term of calculus
Intermediate theory coursework taken at Yale
Departmental evaluation of transferred economics credit toward the major
majors.note: Economics is the practical substitute for Yale's nonexistent undergraduate business degree and is fully open to transfers, though the department decides case by case which outside econ courses count toward the major.

note: Yale is the exception among these three: transfer admission is NOT decided by major or school. Applicants apply to Yale College as a single unit, do not select an undergraduate school, and declare a major only after enrolling (by the end of sophomore year). Yale has no undergraduate business, nursing, or separately-admitted engineering school. The real constraint is volume — a very small cohort enrolls each year (34 in fall 2025) — plus Yale's residency rule that at least 18 course credits must be earned at Yale, which caps transferable credit at roughly two years.
